subject: Agriculture
title: Norman Borlaug's Mission
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Norman Borlaug's Mission.

hook.text: Norman Borlaug, an Iowa farm boy, spent decades breeding wheat in Mexico. He saved a billion lives.

buildup.text: In the 1940s, the Rockefeller Foundation sent Borlaug to Mexico to fight wheat rust disease.

discovery.text: Borlaug crossed thousands of wheat varieties, selecting for disease resistance and high yield simultaneously.

twist.text: Mexican farmers initially rejected his new seeds. He had to prove them in the field, row by painful row.

climax.text: By 1963, Mexico went from wheat importer to wheat exporter. Borlaug's varieties changed a nation.

punchline.text: One scientist, one crop, a billion people fed.

quiz.question: What crop did Norman Borlaug spend decades improving?
